newsitem.title: UK: Smaller Novorossiisk pipeline reopens, Tuapse shut.
newsitem.headline: Smaller Novorossiisk pipeline reopens, Tuapse shut.

text.p: The smaller of two pipelines feeding Russia's leading oil export terminal at Novorossiisk on the Black Sea reopened early on Wednesday after maintenance work was completed, a shipping source said.
But the main pipeline, with a capacity of about 660,000 barrels per day (bpd), was expected to remain shut until Thursday, the source added.
The smaller line started pumping crude again at 0200 (local time) on Wednesday at a rate of about 70,000 bpd. At 0600 (local time) there was about 481,000 barrels in tank at the terminal.
Berthings resumed late on Tuesday after an eight-hour suspension due to heavy swell, allowing a small crude tanker to start loading at berth two.
Vessels were unable to berth at the Black Sea port of Tuapse on Wednesday, however, due to heavy rain and high seas.
Odessa and Ventspils on the Baltic were operating normally, the shipping source said.
